obligation: FCC CPNI rules
basis: The rules bind telecommunications carriers as defined in 47 U.S.C. 153 and include interconnected VoIP providers (47 CFR 64.2003(o)). Each carrier subsidiary (main operating company, AQ-01, AQ-02, AQ-03) provides local exchange, interexchange and wholesale common carrier services and interconnected VoIP lines. No size threshold. Not applicable within the rule: 64.2010(h), because the company provides no CMRS. Broadband usage data is not CPNI after Ohio Telecom Ass'n v. FCC (6th Cir. 2025), but broadband counts as a communications-related service for marketing approvals. The current 64.2011 is in force; the 2023 amendments remain delayed. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: FCC outage reporting
basis: Wireline (4.9(f)), interconnected VoIP (4.9(g)), SS7 provider for 14 rural carriers (4.9(d)) and LEC tandem facilities (4.9(b)); PSAP and 988 notices (4.9(h), (i)); DIRS (4.18). Thresholds are outage-based, not size-based

obligation: CALEA system security and integrity
basis: Each carrier subsidiary transmits or switches wire or electronic communications as a common carrier for hire (47 U.S.C. 1001(8)(A)). AQ-03 closed on 2026-05-15, so its SSI policies were due for refiling within 90 days (1.20005(a)). The January 2025 declaratory ruling was rescinded on 2025-11-20 (90 FR 58006); only the codified SSI rules are analyzed. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: FCC submarine cable landing license national-security rules
basis: The company holds no cable landing license and operates no SLTE

obligation: CIRCIA (pending rule)
basis: Final rule not published at intake; counsel's memo lists it as pending; reporting to CISA is voluntary until it takes effect. Rechecked in P03 and P08

obligation: SEC public-company cybersecurity disclosure
basis: Exchange Act registrant, not a smaller reporting company; the FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C. Item 1.05(d) applies because the company is subject to 47 CFR 64.2011. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: Covered 911 service provider rules
basis: 911 routing to PSAPs is provided by state and regional NG911 system service providers, not the company. Whether originating-provider duties in the 2026 NG911 reliability order (91 FR 42794) reach the company is under review by Regulatory Affairs with counsel, outside this register

obligation: Emergency Alert System rules
basis: No video or broadcast service

obligation: HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The company signs no business associate agreements, and SL-2 terms prohibit storing PHI

obligation: Payment card data security (contractual)
citation: Card brand rules through the processor agreement
basis: Card data is tokenized by the payment processor; duties are contractual and are not analyzed in these deliverables

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; IT general controls over billing, ERP and payroll are tested by the SOX program and not repeated here

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (worked example)
basis: The company holds personal information of Florida residents (online credentials and account data), including its data security (501.171(2)) and disposal (501.171(8)) duties. Florida is the worked example for state law

obligation: Breach notification and data security laws of other states
citation: Statutes of Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina and each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Customers in four states and seasonal or former residents of other states; notify under the law of each state of residence, using counsel's state matrix

obligation: Federal contract reporting clauses (covered telecommunications, Kaspersky, FASCSA)
basis: About 140 federal agency contracts include the three clauses

obligation: Recording consent (worked example)
basis: Care calls and SL-2 recordings use an all-party consent announcement in every state; agent assist (AI-002) transcribes care calls. Florida is the worked example

obligation: Sanctions screening before any ransom payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; the cyber policy also requires insurer approval before any ransom payment

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: Section 5 excludes common carriers subject to the Communications Act (15 U.S.C. 45(a)(2)); counsel reads that as limited to common carrier services, so chatbot statements about broadband plans and prices are in reach

obligation: Fair Credit Reporting Act adverse action duties
basis: Applies where consumer report data is an input to deposit or decline decisions at account opening; counsel confirms at council review

obligation: Federal equal employment opportunity laws (Title VII disparate impact)
basis: The AQ-03 HR system feature ranked job applicants; counsel reviews adverse impact before any re-enable

obligation: State public service commission rules on suspension of regulated voice service
citation: Rules of each state commission where they apply
basis: The collections model orders the suspension work queue for regulated voice service; counsel reviews which state rules apply

obligation: Client agreements for SL-1 and SL-2 (assurance reports, notice and availability terms)
basis: SL-1 clients receive an annual SOC 2 Type 2 report and 24-hour incident notice; SL-2 notice terms vary by contract, and its buyers request a SOC 2 Type 2 report

obligation: Enterprise, government and wholesale customer contracts
basis: 1,900 enterprise and government contracts with CPNI terms and dedicated representatives (the 64.2010(g) business customer exemption), availability SLAs, and wholesale and SS7 transport agreements

obligation: Cyber insurance policy terms
basis: Incident notice to the insurer and insurer approval before any ransom payment
